accessibility.text: For me to survive, which material thing has to continue to exist?
Continuous Ship ≠ Reconstructed Ship
The problem, though, is that these three claims are inconsistent. This is due to the transitivity of identity: if A=B, and B=C, then A=C.
What’s the best way out of this paradox?
Original Ship = Continuous Ship

One natural thought is that we should reject the claim that Original Ship is the same as Reconstructed Ship. On this view, if you find all of the parts that composed some thing, and put them back together, that is not enough to reconstitute the thing. Rather, on this view, material objects survive via a series of causal connections over time, perhaps with the requirement that only relatively small changes at one time are possible.
This is not a story of a ship crashing into itself; so it seems fairly clear that:
We might state this view of the conditions under which material objects continue to exist as follows:
Original Ship = Reconstructed Ship
